title: What If All Earth’s Land Ice Melted?
description:
Sea level would rise by roughly 70 metres—but not overnight.

Complete melting of land ice would raise global mean sea level by about 70 metres over very long timescales.

Floating sea ice contributes little directly when it melts; Greenland and Antarctica contain most of the land-ice potential.

Antarctica alone contains enough ice to raise sea level by roughly 57 metres.
